![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14224622/assets/920aca572a3b6fc828d6c37246b348aa2b017d1bc4e022ea06c12d0fa09ad6ee.png)

Consider the finite region bounded by the curves $x=(1-y)^{2}$ and $y=\sqrt{1-x},$ as shown above. Calculate the volume of the solid generated when this region is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $x$-axis.
question.worked_solution:
First, we write the second function in terms $y$:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\sqrt{1-x} \\ {y}^{2} & =1-x \\ x & =1-{y}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, let $f(y)=1-{y}^{2}$ and $g(y)=(1-y)^{2}.$

We start by determining the points where the curves intersect by solving the following equation for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(y) & =g(y) \\ 1-{y}^{2} & =(1-y)^{2} \\ 1-{y}^{2} & =1-2y+{y}^{2} \\ 2{y}^{2}-2y & =0 \\ 2y(y-1) & =0 \\ y & =0,1\end{aligned}
$$

So, we need to integrate from $y=0$ to $y=1.$ 

Now, let's draw our usual horizontal arrow through the region to determine the left and right functions.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14224622/assets/02e6b4204b1edf682dd332e28830dc84aa0e41d3728c66442d777f6fe9daccfc.png)

The horizontal arrow 

- *enters* the region through the left function $x=g(y)=(1-y)^{2},$ and

- *leaves* through the right function $x=f(y)=1-{y}^{2}.$

Therefore, using the shell method, the volume of the solid can be found as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =2\pi {\int }_{c}^{d}y([\text{right}]-[\text{left}])\,\text{d}y \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}y([1-{y}^{2}]-[(1-y)^{2}])\text{d}y \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}y([1-{y}^{2}]-[1-2y+{y}^{2}])\text{d}y \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}y(2y-2{y}^{2})\text{d}y \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}(2{y}^{2}-2{y}^{3})\text{d}y \\  & =4\pi ({\int }_{0}^{1}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y-{\int }_{0}^{1}{y}^{3}\text{d}y) \\  & =4\pi ({\frac{{y}^{3}}{3}|}_{0}^{1}-{\frac{{y}^{4}}{4}|}_{0}^{1}) \\  & =4\pi ((\frac{1}{3}-0)-(\frac{1}{4}-0)) \\  & =4\pi (\frac{1}{12}) \\  & =\frac{\pi }{3}\end{aligned}
$$
